dedupe_keys.name: eed earth energy designer borehole heat exchanger design software

description: EED, the Earth Energy Designer, is a PC program for designing vertical borehole heat exchangers for ground source heat pump systems and borehole thermal storage. The product page read on 2026-09-26 lists as developers Blocon together with researchers from Chalmers University and Lund University, and says EED handles one borehole up to large systems of 1,200 boreholes and annual loads from a few MWh to several TWh. It is based on g-functions from numerical simulation (SBM), computes brine temperatures from monthly loads, and since version 4 also from hourly loads, with databases of ground thermal properties, pipe materials and heat carrier fluids, 800 borehole patterns and an optimisation list. Coverage is any site; the interface supports 34 languages. The current version 4.4 is dated 23 May 2026; manuals in PDF, example files as a zip download and papers are on the page, and updates come through a link received when ordering, so the software is a paid commercial product. Caveats: EED is a sizing tool based on precomputed g-functions, and very large or complex fields call for more detailed analyses afterwards, as the page says. Simulation uses are capacity planning and optimisation of borehole fields that supply heat pumps or thermal storage in district heating and cooling schemes. Related records: model-geothermos models geothermal systems, and data-western-switzerland-ground-source-heat-pump-potential maps ground source potential.
